If you live in Greer, you know the yellow film that settles on cars and porches every spring. What fewer people plan for is that the same pollen works its way into window tracks, vent covers and the entry floor, and it keeps coming back for weeks. The best time to prepare is now, in late November, when you still have time to book a team and split the work into small jobs. Here is how we would plan spring house cleaning in Greer, SC from the winter side.

Think of spring cleaning in Greer as three kinds of work: the dust and pollen jobs that must be finished before the season, the deep jobs that only happen once a year, such as kitchen degreasing and bathroom grout, and the upkeep that carries you through to summer. Separating them keeps the list from feeling endless, and it tells you which jobs to hand to a crew and which to do between other plans. A family with two kids and a dog will have a different list from a retired couple, so write yours from your own home rather than from a generic template. We have also found that people who book early get their pick of weekdays, which matters if you want the team there while you are at work.

Here is how to build the plan.

Step one: decide what spring cleaning means for your house

For most Greer homes it is not a total overhaul. It is a short list of jobs that get skipped during the year and get worse in pollen season. Write yours on one sheet before the holidays, then you can attach dates.

  • Window tracks and sills, inside and the glass you can reach.
  • Vent covers, ceiling fans and the tops of door frames.
  • Baseboards, especially along exterior walls.
  • Entry area: mats, door frame and the floor where shoes land.
  • Bathroom grout and the base of the toilet.
  • Kitchen degreasing: stovetop, hood and cabinet fronts.
  • Closets and bedrooms: wash bedding, vacuum under beds.

A winter-to-spring timeline

WhenWhat to do
Late fall to early winterWrite the list, book your estimate visit and choose a start date
January and FebruaryClosets, storage and the deeper kitchen and bathroom jobs, while the weather is cool and windows stay closed
Late February to early MarchVents, fans, baseboards and windows, before pollen is airborne
Pollen seasonKeep up a lighter routine: wipe entries, vacuum often, wash bedding weekly

Doing the deep jobs before pollen arrives is the point. If you clean windows in April, the dust blows back in the next day.

Why Greer homes need an extra look

Greer sits across Greenville and Spartanburg counties, with ZIP codes 29650, 29651 and 29652, and its housing runs from historic homes near Downtown Greer and Trade Street to newer neighborhoods near GSP Airport and the BMW plant. Older homes often have more trim and window detail, and newer ones usually have larger open rooms with lots of floor. Red clay tracked in from yards stains light carpet and the grout between tiles, so both styles benefit from a pre-spring clean. We are based here, so this is the house we clean most.

What a crew handles and what you can keep

Our Greer house cleaning page lists everything a visit includes. A visit from our team covers kitchen counters, sink and stovetop cleaned and sanitized, appliance fronts, bathrooms, floors vacuumed and mopped by hand, dusting, beds made, trash emptied, baseboards and door frames, and light switches. Details are on our house cleaning in Greer page and the broader house cleaning and maid service page. If your list includes cabinets or heavy buildup, ask about deep cleaning as a first visit, then recurring service to maintain it.

What we would keep for yourself: decluttering, sorting seasonal clothes and decisions about what to donate. Those take your judgment, and the cleaning goes faster when they are done.

Start small, but start

A note on what the first walkthrough looks like. When we visit before an estimate, we look at the rooms you named on your list, check the condition of floors and baseboards, ask about pets and allergies, and write down anything unusual, such as a stained grout line or a window that sticks. That is how we give you a realistic time and an exact price. It also gives you a chance to ask questions about products if someone in the house is sensitive to strong smells. Greer homeowners often tell us the walkthrough clarified their own list, because it is easier to see what really needs work when someone walks through with you. You do not need to finish the list in one weekend. Choose two items per week from January and you will be done before the first pollen warning. faqs: When should I schedule spring house cleaning in Greer?
Planning in late fall or winter leaves room to choose a date before the March and April rush. Deep jobs are easiest to finish before pollen is in the air.
Does pollen change how I should clean?
Yes. Pollen collects in window tracks, vents, fans and entries, so those spots deserve attention before the season and light upkeep during it.
Should my first visit be a deeper clean?
Often yes. The first visit is usually deeper so the home reaches a maintenance standard, and recurring visits keep it there.
